summary: No new receipt this turn; I corrected a stale self-answer instead. The gap asking whether the silently created two-server change lets running nodes hold disjoint majorities and elect two leaders was still recorded as 'partly answered, not yet executed', even though the dual-majority receipts settled it. It is now answered and resolved affirmatively with those receipts: the two-server change commits on the stale leader plus the promoted caught-up nonvoter while the old voter is partitioned, the old majority elects a leader in a higher term while the stale leader still leads its own configuration, and after healing the committed entry is replaced by the new leader's entry, leaving different logs and different applied state on the two sides (witness indices 2, 3/6 and 7). The answer also keeps the earlier reasoning that the direct route stays impossible — a voter that never receives the entry is strictly behind and is refused by voters that hold it — which is precisely why the construction needs the entry to commit without one old voter, made possible by the promoted nonvoter and by the new configuration entering the commitment on append.
